test_title: PYST 27: SSC CGL 2025 Tier-I Similar Paper - English (Held On: 20th Sep 2025 Shift 3)
subject: english
question:
Choose the correct meaning of idiom:

Heap coals of fire on someone’s head
solution:
The correct answer is '2' i.e. Shame through generosity .

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The idiom **“Heap coals of fire on someone's head”** is used to describe the act of responding to someone's unkindness by showing kindness or generosity, thereby making the person feel ashamed.
 
• This phrase originates from biblical references and implies overcoming evil with good.
 
• In this context, **Option 2**, “Shame through generosity,” correctly captures the meaning of the idiom.

Correct sentence: *When someone is rude to you, heap coals of fire on their head by being kind and generous in return.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Other meanings of the options:**

 
 
• **Option 1:** “Insult openly” – This does not align with the idiom's meaning as it implies direct disrespect.
 
• **Option 3:** “Punish severely” – This is incorrect as the idiom does not involve punishment but rather kindness.
 
• **Option 4:** “Encourage rivalry” – This is unrelated to the idiom's meaning.
